lessons.title: Story Time: Rousseau's Jungle Inspired Tale
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss the setting of a jungle-themed story.
success_criteria: I can describe the jungle setting.
I can name an animal in the story.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a Rousseau jungle painting and predict a story.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a jungle-animal-themed story, modelling discussion of setting.
lessons.independent_task: Children describe the jungle setting and name animals featured.
key_questions: What does the jungle look like?
What animal is in the story?

differentiation.greater_depth: Describe the setting in full sentences

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of setting description — evidence for ENG.R2.

lessons.title: Number Review: Counting and Comparing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting and comparing skills to an animal art context.
success_criteria: I can count a set of animal pictures.
I can compare two sets.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting and comparing sets of animal picture repeats (as in Warhol-style repeated images).
lessons.independent_task: Children count and compare sets of repeated animal images, recording which has more/fewer.
key_questions: How many animals in this set?
Which set has more?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting and comparing consolidation — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Count and compare two sets of objects at home.

lessons.title: Studying Henri Rousseau's Jungle Paintings
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of Rousseau's painting style.
success_criteria: I can describe what I notice in Rousseau's painting.
I can name a colour or shape he used.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a Henri Rousseau jungle painting.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss Rousseau's style — layered leaves, bold colours, hidden animals.
lessons.independent_task: Children describe what they notice in a Rousseau painting, recording their observations.
key_questions: What animal can you find hidden in the painting?
What colours has the artist used?

differentiation.support: Point to and describe one feature
differentiation.greater_depth: Describe multiple features and give an opinion

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational and descriptive skill studying an artist — evidence for ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Look at more jungle paintings together if possible.

lessons.title: Writing About a Painting
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write sentences describing what they see in a painting.
success_criteria: I can write what I see in the painting.
I can use a describing word.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing descriptive sentences about a painting.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences describing a Rousseau or Warhol animal artwork.
key_questions: What can you see in the painting?
What colours are used?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive writing about visual art — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share painting descriptions with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Describe a picture or painting at home.

lessons.title: Symmetry in Animal Patterns
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify symmetry in animal patterns (e.g. butterfly wings, tiger stripes).
success_criteria: I can say if an animal pattern is symmetrical.
I can create a symmetrical animal pattern.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a butterfly picture and discuss its symmetry.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model identifying symmetry in animal patterns and creating a symmetrical butterfly using paint blot technique.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a symmetrical animal pattern using the paint blot (fold and press) technique.
key_questions: Is this pattern symmetrical?
How did you make yours symmetrical?

differentiation.greater_depth: Create a more detailed symmetrical design

lessons.assessment_notes: Note symmetry understanding and application — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.home_link: Look for symmetry in animals or nature at home.

lessons.title: Creating a Rousseau-Style Jungle Scene
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a layered jungle scene inspired by Rousseau.
success_criteria: I can layer leaf shapes to create depth.
I can hide an animal in my scene.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a layered jungle scene using cut-out leaf shapes of varying sizes.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own layered jungle scene, hiding an animal within it.
key_questions: How did you create depth?
Where is your hidden animal?

differentiation.greater_depth: Add multiple layers and hidden animals

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe application of an artist's technique — evidence for ART.1/ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Class 'spot the animal' game using the jungle scenes.
lessons.home_link: Look for hidden patterns in leaves or plants at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Jungle Animal Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read jungle animal words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read jungle animal words.
I can read a sentence about the jungle.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending jungle animal words (e.g. 'tiger', 'snake', 'monkey').
lessons.independent_task: Children read jungle-themed word and sentence cards.
key_questions: Can you blend this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading jungle animal words over the week.

lessons.title: Repeated Addition: Warhol-Style Grids
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use repeated addition to find a total in a grid.
success_criteria: I can add equal groups together.
I can find the total in a grid.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model finding the total of a grid of repeated images (e.g. 3 rows of 4 animal pictures) using repeated addition.
lessons.independent_task: Children find totals of repeated image grids using repeated addition, recording number sentences.
resources_needed: Grid worksheets with repeated animal images
key_questions: How many animals in each row?
What is the total using repeated addition?

differentiation.support: Use grids within 10 with counting support
differentiation.greater_depth: Use grids within 20 and link to early multiplication

lessons.assessment_notes: Record early multiplication understanding via repeated addition — evidence for MATHS.N2/N3.
lessons.home_link: Find repeated groups of objects at home and add them.

lessons.title: Studying Andy Warhol's Repeated Animal Prints
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of Warhol's pop-art style.
success_criteria: I can describe what I notice in Warhol's work.
I can say how it's different from Rousseau's style.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a Warhol animal print (e.g. his endangered species series).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss Warhol's style — bold colours, repetition, simplified shapes — comparing to Rousseau's style.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare Warhol and Rousseau's styles, recording one similarity and one difference.
key_questions: How is this different from Rousseau's painting?
What do you notice about the colours?

differentiation.support: Point to and describe one feature
differentiation.greater_depth: Give a detailed comparison with opinion

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative art analysis skill — evidence for ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the two artists' contrasting styles.
lessons.home_link: Look at more pop-art examples together if possible.

lessons.title: Presenting My Animal Artwork
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present their animal artwork and explain their inspiration.
success_criteria: I can describe my artwork.
I can say which artist inspired me.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the artists studied this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation about artwork.
lessons.independent_task: Children present their jungle scene or repeated print artwork to a small group.
key_questions: Which artist inspired your work?
What technique did you use?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and art reflection progress — evidence for ENG.SL1/ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Present your artwork to your family.

lessons.title: Fractions in Art: Colouring Halves and Quarters
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply fraction knowledge to colour shapes accurately.
success_criteria: I can colour half of a shape.
I can colour a quarter of a shape.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model colouring exactly half and a quarter of shapes, linking to an art pattern.
lessons.independent_task: Children colour shapes to show half/quarter accurately, creating a simple patterned artwork.
key_questions: Have you coloured exactly half?
How do you know it's a quarter?

differentiation.support: Colour halves only with a folded guide
differentiation.greater_depth: Colour halves and quarters accurately without guides

lessons.assessment_notes: Record fraction application to a practical/creative task — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Colour half of a shape at home.

lessons.title: Creating My Own Repeated Animal Print
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a repeated print artwork in the style of Warhol.
success_criteria: I can print the same animal shape multiple times.
I can use bold colours.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Warhol's repeated print style from Wednesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model printing the same animal stamp/stencil multiple times using different bold colours.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own repeated animal print artwork using bold colours.
key_questions: What colours will you repeat with?
How many times will you print your animal?

differentiation.greater_depth: Create a grid layout with varied colour combinations

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe application of a repeated print technique — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.home_link: Try a simple print pattern at home using safe household objects.

lessons.title: Artists Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about the artists studied this week.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question about an artist.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about the two artists, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the artists.
key_questions: What did Rousseau paint?
Why did Warhol repeat his images?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on the artists you learned about.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Number, Symmetry, Fractions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply number, symmetry, and fraction skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can count and compare.
I can identify symmetry.
I can find half/quarter.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of number, symmetry, and fractions.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
key_questions: How many is this?
Is this symmetrical?
What is half of this?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 26 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/N4/GEO.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising symmetry and fractions over the weekend.

lessons.title: Animal Art Gallery and Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to reflect on and present their animal art from the week.
success_criteria: I can talk about my favourite piece.
I can name the artist who inspired me.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all art techniques used this week (layering, printing, symmetry).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss reflecting on and presenting artwork in a gallery format.
lessons.independent_task: Children set up and present a mini gallery of their animal art from the week.
key_questions: Which piece are you most proud of?
Which artist inspired you most?

differentiation.support: Point to work and name the artist
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the process and reasoning behind choices

lessons.assessment_notes: Note reflective language and artist knowledge recall — evidence for ART.1/ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Whole-class gallery walk of animal art.
lessons.home_link: Show your favourite piece of art from this week to your family.
